headline: Enhanced Asset Management sees REA Group as compelling value below $200, expecting ~15% EPS growth in FY27 despite housing headwinds
reasoning: Bowen Hosking argues that consensus analysts were overly bearish on REA Group's listing volumes, forecasting up to 8-10% declines for FY27 due to housing slowdown and tax changes. However, Enhanced Asset Management's thesis is that upcoming CGT and family trust legislative changes will actually drive forced selling, creating listing volume tailwinds. REA is guiding for another double-digit revenue increase in FY27. The business has strong pricing power and a dominant network-effect platform where buyers and sellers reinforce each other's presence on the platform. At a sub-30x PE with ~15% EPS growth expected over five years, Hosking views any price below $200 as good value, and dismisses AI disruption risk given sellers are transacting their most expensive asset and won't take shortcuts.
quote: this one's now I think it's a sub 30 times PE for a business that will just continue to pump out 1,015% EPs growth over the next five years. There's obviously the threat of AR disruption that people have, um, you know, theorised a bit for Aria, but but this is a platform business, right? And and it's a business where people are selling their most expensive asset. They're not going to take any shortcuts here. It's a bit of a circular, um, theory in terms of the way that this business is going to continue to dominate in the sense that buyers will continue to look to, to continue to browse where they think a majority of the listings are. And at the moment, that's on Aria, of course. And the sellers are going to sell where the majority of the buyers are looking, which is on Aria, and it just keeps kind of circulating on itself. So I mean, the the way that the listing platform continues to grow and demand are really struggling to, to kind of implement anything that's going to take away that market share from Aria. Um, yeah. We think anything below $200 is pretty good value here.
episode_title: Positive results the market could be missing

headline: Bowen Hosking sees REA Group's headline profit decline as obscuring underlying business strength, with fears around housing slowdown and AI disruption overdone
reasoning: REA Group's net profit fell 19% and the stock derated significantly from around $210-220 to $130. Hosking's thesis heading into the result was that consensus expectations of 8-10% listing volume declines for FY27 due to CGT changes and a housing slowdown were too pessimistic. He believed many of the tax changes would actually accelerate listings as vendors tried to get ahead of CGT changes, contrary to the prevailing bearish view. The India impairment was a known one-off. Hosking suggests the market has been overly focused on external headwinds.
quote: Again, it's one of those ones on face value. There's probably a lot of external headwinds that, you know, investors can focus on. That's I mean, largely why we're seeing that the share price drop from sort of two, 10 to 20 all the way down to I think it got to about $130 a couple of months ago. Um, look, the, the we've seen saw a few expectations going into the result that, uh, housing prices were going to really negatively impact the listing volumes and especially with the tax changes that are coming through. Um, you know, the thesis for a lot of analysts out there, was that okay? Uh, there's a there's a housing slowdown, and we're going to see a big impact on listing volumes for RA. I think that's for a few analysts had up to up to 8 to 10% listing volume forecast decreases for FY 27. And what our thesis was heading into. The result was actually a lot of these tax changes that were going to force people to to put their house on the market, whether they're trying to get in before, um, the CGT changes come through.

headline: Bowen Hosking views ResMed's result as strong and sees near-term share price weakness as a buying opportunity ahead of margin recovery in H2 FY27
reasoning: Hosking views ResMed's result as broadly strong despite some moving parts including the Matrix Care sale and the Astral recall impacting US device sales. Stripping out the recall, the core business grew 8% in the US, in line with historical performance. Cash flow generation was strong. Near-term margin pressure from freight and electrical component costs is expected to weigh on Q1 FY27, but as price increases are pushed through and inflation normalises, margins are expected to tick up meaningfully in H2 FY27. The 5-7% revenue growth guidance for FY27 was in line with expectations once the Matrix Care sale is accounted for.
quote: We think the result was pretty strong. Um, there's obviously a few moving parts in this one. They've had the sale of their matrix care business, which is um, obviously impacting uh, their, their outlook. Um, the, the guidance is a little bit, uh, under where we sort of expected it because of that before the sale. Um, but obviously, you know, analysts are very aware of that. So the 5 to 7% revenue growth guidance for FY 27 is, is about what we expected it to come in. Um, there's again moving parts that have had the Astral Week recall, which has sort of affected their uh, um, sort of end of life, uh, ventilator business over in the US. Um, but look on Face Valley, you look at the US to buy sales at 6% and you think, okay, maybe that's a little bit soft, but when you strip that out, that recoil out, which, um, you know, they, they seem like they've gone under control. The core business grew 8% over there, which is in line with sort of how they've been performing over the past couple of years. We think it's a pretty strong result. Their cash flow generation has been really strong. Um, but Q1 next quarter, what they're guiding for for Q1 27 is potentially a little bit weak. Um, you're seeing some freight freight cost increases and some increases in their electrical components that might impact gross margins a little bit in the first quarter. Um, we think that's probably a bit of an opportunity. We expect the share price to be maybe down a little bit today, a little bit weak. Um, but look, as they push these price increases through and we get a little bit of a normalization in the inflationary environment, we expect that margins will really tick up in probably the back half of FY 27, which will be a really good environment for the business.

headline: Enhanced Asset Management bullish on high-quality growth companies heading into reporting season given low expectations
reasoning: Hosking notes that macro factors including inflation and Middle East issues have weighed on sentiment, but expectations for high-quality growth businesses have been reset low. He expects volatile price moves in reporting season as has been the case in recent seasons, but is fundamentally bullish on the companies in his portfolio. He sees the low-expectation environment as an opportunity for quality growth names.
quote: Look it's um it's an interesting situation we're going into at the moment. You've obviously got a lot of macro factors that are, um, impacting companies results. And I mean, particularly over the last probably 3 to 6 months. We'll see, you know, how companies have been able to navigate the inflationary environment and obviously all the issues in the Middle East. But look, we're pretty positive on a lot of the growth companies that have been rated pretty significantly. I mean, we're heading into a reporting season where expectations are actually pretty low for a lot of the the high quality growth businesses that we like to follow and we like to invest in.
